name: STEM short time-series clustering
title: Which few-year spending shapes are real, and which are noise?
what: Fixes 50 possible shapes in advance, assigns each program's short path to its closest shape, and tests which shapes are over-full.
pick_line: Text enrichment per real shape: which description terms are over-represented, as STEM does with gene annotations.
data: SYNTHETIC mock ZBB budgets (Corning-like and Morgan Stanley-like); answer key used only for scoring
one: Says which few-year shapes are real (5–7 of 50) where k-means always finds clusters, even in noise.

picture.la: Usual tool: k-means returns 10 and 5 clusters on pure noise
picture.lb: STEM: 0–1 real shapes on noise, 5–7 on the mocks

findings.h: It tells real shapes from noise; k-means cannot.
findings.t: With each program's years shuffled (pure noise), STEM finds 1 significant shape of 50 on the Corning-like mock (29 programs) and 0 on the MS-like mock. On the real mocks: 7 shapes (329 of 778 programs) and 5 (584 of 1,404). K-means on the same noise still returns 10 and 5 clusters, with silhouettes 0.184 and 0.242 against 0.244 and 0.377 on the real mocks.
findings.note: Pre-registered pass bar (0–1 shapes on noise) met on both mocks. In the paper's own simulation (20 seeds) STEM recovered the 3 planted shapes every time with no false positives, and 2 of 20 pure-noise runs gave one false shape.

chart.la: Usual tool vs STEM, real and shuffled

findings.h: Reading budget as a second measurement puts more programs on their true shape.
findings.t: Exploratory (not pre-registered): giving STEM the budget as a same-year replicate of the actual raises the programs in real shapes from 329 to 477 (Corning-like) and 584 to 830 (MS-like). The share of those sitting on their noise-free shape rises from 0.31 to 0.47 and from 0.75 to 0.82.
findings.note: Noise-free true levels put 756 of 778 and 1,193 of 1,404 programs in real shapes: observation noise hides most of the structure.

findings.h: It finds planted groups only partly, and k-means with the same k does as well.
findings.t: Best F1 against the planted co-moving groups: STEM beats silhouette-chosen k-means (k = 2) by ≥ 0.05 on 3 of 4 Corning-like groups and 1 of 3 MS-like groups (pre-registered pass), e.g. display tradeoff 0.49 vs 0.18, equity activity 0.48 vs 0.24. Given the same number of clusters as STEM, k-means matches or beats it on 5 of 7. Segment × function cells beat both on 5 of 7 (the generator places groups by archetype).
findings.note: The late-rising AI-demand group is not one of STEM's real shapes (F1 0.18). Power: a shape needs about 80 programs (10% of the book) at noise σ = 0.10 to be detected 90% of the time; 40 programs, 5%.

chart.la: Power by group size and noise

findings.h: It does not flag 'says growth, actually declining' better than a slope.
findings.t: Among programs stated as grow or transform, membership of a real falling shape catches 3 of 6 planted mismatches with 68 flags (Corning-like) and 3 of 25 with 7 flags (MS-like). The most negative OLS slopes, same number of flags, catch 4 and 5.
findings.note: Pre-registered bar (precision ≥ OLS at matched count) failed on both mocks.
